source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — Montenegrin Banking Association, SEPA section
why_relevant: Industry body coordinating the eleven commercial banks through SEPA and instant-payment migration; a natural candidate for the NASO (National Adherence Support Organisation) function and for circulating participant-facing explanatory material and readiness timelines that never appear in supervision channels.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco SEE — ChipCard regional card processor and Montenegrin bank card/POS deployments
why_relevant: Vendor-side visibility into who actually runs card issuing/acquiring processing and POS estates for Montenegrin banks. ChipCard (ASEE-owned) acts as a regional processor serving Montenegrin bank acquiring (ATM, POS, e-commerce); ASEE also supplied POS platform migrations to NLB Montenegro. Vendor press releases reveal switch/processing arrangements that no regulator publishes.

source_name: Commercial bank general terms & payment tariffs (e.g. Hipotekarna banka Opšti uslovi poslovanja; Erste ME SEPA blog)
why_relevant: Participant-side confirmation of scheme adoption: general terms and tariff books state which payment schemes a bank supports, cut-off times, instant-payment limits and effective dates of change. Reading these across the eleven banks reconstructs actual rollout status independently of central announcements.

source_name: EU Delegation to Montenegro / EEAS — Montenegro operationally part of SEPA
why_relevant: EU-side confirmation of operational SEPA status and of the accession conditionality attached to payments alignment. Useful as an independent, dated corroboration layer for milestone claims and as a pointer to EU acquis chapters driving future payment mandates.

source_name: SeeNews — Montenegro payments infrastructure coverage
why_relevant: Regional business wire that dates Montenegrin payment-infrastructure milestones in English — the CBCG–EPC licensing agreement, the RTS/X new-generation national payment system go-live on 26 May 2025, and instant-payment launch steps. Convenient English cross-check for local-language claims.

source_name: Local general media cluster covering payment mandates (RTNK, Sjever CG, aktuelno.me, antenam.net, MINA, CdM, Vijesti/B92 regional)
why_relevant: Where the participant-facing compliance clock actually got reported: banks must make funds available within ten seconds 24/7/365, EUR 1,000 cap, an eight-day deadline to comply with basic rules after infrastructure establishment, nine months for verification-of-payee and eighteen months for batch instruction verification. These transposed deadline numbers surface in press before consolidated regulation.

source_name: NBS IPS QR standard (Serbia) — regional comparator for national payment QR
why_relevant: Not a Montenegrin source, but the reference implementation a Montenegrin payment-QR standard would most plausibly be modelled on (or interoperate with): published QR generator/validator, element definitions and scheme documentation for instant-payment QR. Useful as a template and as a watch-point for cross-border QR interoperability in the region.

source_name: CBCG FinTech Hub — Regulatorni inovacijski centar
why_relevant: The formal channel through which fintechs and PSPs (domestic and foreign) present innovations and request CBCG interpretations. Its news/publications section reveals which product categories operators are pushing and what the supervisor is signalling back — an operator-intent proxy that precedes licensing.

source_name: PaySpot ME d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution presenting itself as the first PI registered in Montenegro; ~60+ physical locations, bill payment, domestic remittance, 'uplata pazara' cash-collection for merchants, e-commerce. Its service pages and terms are a primary operator-side read on obligations and product direction.

source_name: Presto Pay d.o.o. Podgorica — Opšti uslovi poslovanja za pružanje platnih usluga
why_relevant: A licensed PI publishing its full payment-services terms of business — exactly the operator's own articulation of statutory duties (information duties, execution times, complaint handling, fees). Best single artefact for tracking how ME PSPs translate regulation into customer-facing obligations.

source_name: Alta Pay Group d.o.o. Podgorica (Alta Pay Crna Gora)
why_relevant: Serbian Alta group's Montenegrin PI arm; group communications explicitly describe the ME expansion, that Alta Pay Podgorica and Montenegro Transfers Podgorica sit in the same group, and that Montenegro Transfers is the sole Western Union agent. Group-level PR is where licence and product news for this operator actually appears.

source_name: Alta Pay Crna Gora — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Operator-controlled channel where ME payment firms post licence, partnership and product news and hiring signals (compliance/AML roles indicate regulatory workload). LinkedIn is heavily bot-defended for automated collection.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — financial/company profiles
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of ME company data; the ALTA PAY GROUP profile gave registered address, incorporation date (2019-10-28), director, owner and NACE activity. Useful to enrich the operator map without repeated registry queries.

source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka) — Opšti uslovi poslovanja za platni promet i izdavanje i upotrebu kartica (PDF)
why_relevant: Bank-as-PSP terms document with an explicit clause on amending the general conditions; a dated version (July 2026 per search snippet) makes it a usable tracker of how ME payment-service providers implement notice periods and new statutory duties. Serves as the benchmark text non-bank PSPs mirror.

source_name: RTCG — Ekonomija (national public broadcaster, economy desk)
why_relevant: Public-service coverage of payments milestones; documented the 20 July 2026 go-live of instant payments in ME with all 11 banks on a TIPS Clone platform. Useful for dating market-wide events that reshape PSP product roadmaps.

source_name: CBCG — Finansijski sistem Crne Gore (financial system overview)
why_relevant: Structural map of which institution types exist and who supervises them; anchors the payments operator population against banks, MFIs and other providers, and links onward to per-sector supervision pages.

source_name: CdM (Cafe del Montenegro) — Ekonomija
why_relevant: High-traffic ME news portal that republishes PSP press releases (e.g. PaySpot ME new locations). Corporate-communication carrier for operator expansion news that never reaches an English source.

source_name: Offshore/company-formation advisory pages on Montenegro EMI & PI licensing (Dealable24, N5Bank, PriFinance, Advapay)
why_relevant: These vendors sell ME licence-application services, so they publish (and update) capital thresholds, documentation lists and process timelines faster than official English material. Treat as a lead indicator of foreign interest in ME PI/EMI licences, but low credibility — every claim must be re-verified against CBCG.

source_name: The Fintech Times — Montenegro's Fintech Ecosystem in 2026
why_relevant: One of very few English-language ecosystem overviews of ME fintech; useful for cross-checking actor names and for the international framing of ME payments, but secondary and unverified in this pass.

source_name: Monri Payments (regional omnichannel PSP, WebPay/WSPay)
why_relevant: Regional (HR-based) card-acquiring/gateway provider whose WebPay/WSPay rails and e-commerce plugins are widely used across the Western Balkans; its terms and product pages reveal the technical/compliance stack ME merchants and PSPs plug into. ME-specific presence was not confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka AD Podgorica — Opšti uslovi poslovanja / Tarifa naknada
source_subtype: bank general terms & fee tariff page
why_relevant: First-party regulated-entity publication of general business terms with an explicit 'in application from' date, plus the fee-tariff extract. Version dates evidence statutory pre-notification periods for T&C/fee changes and are the earliest concrete signal that a CBCG rule or payment-services deadline is biting.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — Obavještenja za klijente (client notices, homepage news)
why_relevant: Homepage/news stream carries dated notices such as 'Obavještenje za klijente – Izmjene Opštih uslova poslovanja i Odluke o tarifi naknada'; these notices are the statutory customer pre-notification and carry the effective date of the change.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — Izvještaji (annual/financial reports & disclosures)
why_relevant: Regulated-entity reporting hub; annual reports and public disclosure documents include capital adequacy and risk data required under CBCG/credit-institutions law.

source_name: Addiko Bank AD Podgorica — Finansijski izvještaji / Javno objelodanjivanje podataka
why_relevant: Best-structured Montenegrin bank disclosure archive found: annual, semi-annual and quarterly public disclosures back to 2011, published explicitly under Article 237 of the Law on Credit Institutions and CBCG disclosure regulation. Publication cadence itself is evidence of the reporting deadline regime.

source_name: Crnogorska komercijalna banka (CKB, OTP Group) — Opšti uslovi i dokumenta
source_subtype: bank general terms, lists of conditions, tarifnik
why_relevant: Largest Montenegrin bank. Publishes versioned general terms (payments and card issuance/use with dated validity), lists of conditions for individuals and legal entities with future effective dates, and the tarifnik. Dated 'lista uslova' changes are the clearest customer-notice trail in the market.

source_name: CKB — Finansijski izvještaji / godišnji izvještaji
why_relevant: Annual reports and audited consolidated statements of the market-leading bank, with a long archive (at least back to 2003) usable as a baseline for disclosure-practice change over time.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica — Naknade i opšti uslovi poslovanja (fizička i pravna lica)
why_relevant: Dedicated page pairing fee schedule with general terms, with explicit application dates (e.g. terms for individuals and for legal entities/entrepreneurs in force from 31.03.2025). Direct evidence of the notice-and-effective-date mechanism.
